title: The Magnetic Fields of Starburst Galaxies. I. Identification and Characterization of the Thermal Polarization in the Galactic Disk and Outflow
question: Systematic analysis and separation of the magnetic fields and thermal dust polarization properties in the galactic disk and outflow of nearby starburst galaxies using 53-890 um polarimetric observations.

We also include the polarization spectrum of a heterogeneous cloud (cite: H1999) and the two-component dust temperature (cite: Vaillancourt2008).

recipe.goal: Resample sub-mm maps and apply polarimetric quality cuts
recipe.method: Resample JCMT/POL-2 (to 7.5'') and ALMA (to 0.15'') Stokes maps to Nyquist sampling, rotate polarization angles by 90 deg to obtain B-field orientation, and filter pixels by SNR and polarization fraction thresholds.
assumptions: Observed FIR/sub-mm polarization angle rotated by 90 deg traces the local B-field orientation

recipe.goal: Disentangle disk and outflow components geometrically
recipe.method: Fit Gaussian profiles to Stokes Q and U distributions at 89 um, compute the B-field orientation range PA_B,+/- from the fitted means and standard deviations, compare angular differences with the galaxy tilt angle theta, and assign the larger angular difference to the outflow and smaller to the disk across all wavelengths.
key_parameters: Galaxy tilt angles theta: 64 +/- 1 deg (M82), 52 +/- 1 deg (NGC 253), 140 +/- 2 deg (NGC 2146)

recipe.goal: Compute resolved and integrated polarization fractions and polarization spectra
recipe.method: Compute debiased mean polarization fraction <P^hist> (Eq. 1) and integrated polarization fraction P^int (Eq. 2) for full galaxy, disk, and outflow regions per band, and normalize polarization spectra to 154 um.
key_parameters: Reference wavelength lambda_0 = 154 um for normalized polarization spectra

recipe.goal: Fit total and polarized flux SEDs
recipe.method: Sum Stokes I and PI over full galaxy, disk, and outflow regions and fit single-temperature modified blackbody functions in the 50-250 um wavelength range for M82 and NGC 2146 using MCMC.
assumptions: Single-temperature modified blackbody with dust mass absorption coefficient k_lambda0 = 0.29 m^2 kg^-1 at lambda_0 = 250 um

recipe.goal: Analyze vertical height dependence across the outflow and separate inner/outer outflow spectra
recipe.method: Construct 2D vertical height maps rotated by galaxy tilt angle theta centered on the emission peak at each wavelength, extract Stokes IQU in 2-pixel-wide slots (1 beam), compute vertical profiles and power-law slopes of I, PI, and P^int, and compute separate polarization spectra for inner outflow (within h_peak^PI) and outer outflow (beyond h_peak^PI), comparing them with literature dust models via reduced chi-squared.
assumptions: Galaxy disk lies on the x-y plane and is rotated by tilt angle theta along the z-axis

recipe.goal: Estimate turbulent B-field strengths and energy budget in the outflow
recipe.method: Scale turbulent B-field strength with SFR using B = B_0 * SFR^(0.34+/-0.04) calibrated on M82, then compute turbulent kinetic energy U_K = 0.5 * rho * sigma_v^2, turbulent magnetic energy U_B = B^2 / (8*pi), and plasma parameter beta' = U_K / U_B.
key_parameters: B_0 = 128 uG M_sun^-0.34 yr^-0.34, calibrated from B_M82 = 305 +/- 5 uG and SFR_M82 = 13 M_sun yr^-1
Core depth h_c: 500 pc (M82), 50 pc (NGC 253), 2000 pc (NGC 2146)
assumptions: Turbulent B-field scales as B propto SFR^(0.34+/-0.04) and starburst region depth h_c equals the length of the polarized region along the major axis of the galaxy

score_reason: The mathematical recipes for polarization debiasing, disk/outflow PA separation, MCMC SED fitting (including sampler, priors, chains, and steps), vertical height profiling, and energy budget calculation are clearly specified and the data are public, though exact ALMA image provenance (archive vs Belfiori et al. in prep.) and peak centering coordinates are not explicitly given.
rediscovery_reason: All datasets (SALSA SOFIA/HAWC+ data at galmagfields.com, JCMT/POL-2 M82 data, and ALMA #2018.1.01358.S NGC 253 data) are public, the mathematical formulas and quality cuts are explicitly written out, and the main results are numeric tables of polarization fractions, SED parameters, vertical heights, and energy budgets.
